command.reason: Locate the yellow and white mug, its handle, and the open microwave geometry before approaching.
Approach the yellow and white mug from above, close around its upper body, and lift to verify acquisition.
The closed fingers are empty and the mug remains on the counter; measure its current rim and body for a lower grasp.
Lower the open fingers around the settled mug body, grasp it, then lift for visual confirmation.
The body grasp did not acquire the mug; locate the narrow handle for a grasp across its thickness.
Grasp the yellow handle with the fingers closing across its thin dimension, then lift the mug.
The mug is visibly suspended from its handle. Measure the microwave entrance, floor, and open door to choose a collision-free insertion path.
Bring the held mug in front of the microwave opening and lower it below the roof before insertion.
Insert the mug through the front opening while keeping its base just above the microwave floor.
The mug met the entrance lip; retract slightly, raise its base above the sill, and retry insertion.
Lower the grasp slightly to clear the microwave roof while keeping the mug above the sill, then advance farther inside.
Set the mug down at the opening and withdraw the gripper to assess its position and prepare a lower-profile push farther inside.
Use the closed fingers horizontally to push the protruding handle and slide the upright mug deeper into the microwave.
Withdraw from the microwave to check that the mug and handle clear the door before closing it.
Locate the free edge and hinge of the open door, and check the mug handle clearance for a controlled closing sweep.
Approach the outside face of the open door near its free edge and begin pushing it toward the microwave.
Follow the free edge through its closing arc, sweeping the door toward the microwave front.
Release pressure and inspect the remaining door gap before choosing the final closing contact.
Measure the remaining door angle and handle position so the final push seats the door without pressing on the appliance body.
Press the door near its free edge with the fingers pointed horizontally, then withdraw to verify that it remains closed.
Check whether the door is seated flush and the mug is behind its window after the final push.

scope: Offline measurements, not automatic causal attribution. Raw wrist loads include gravity and dynamics.
